correctness.rationale: With \(z=2\pi|x|^2\), the classical radial Fourier–Laguerre generating function gives eigenvalue \((-1)^j\); the chosen indices \(2,4,6,8\) thus give \(+1\). The exact Laguerre expansion is \(f(x)=e^{-\pi|x|^2}zQ(z)/40320\), with \(Q\) explicitly specified in RESULT.md. Its eight-member rational Sturm chain has variations \(4,4,3,3\) at \(0,73/20,183/50,+\infty\), so a unique positive root \(\rho\) lies strictly in \((73/20,183/50)\). The leading coefficient and \(Q(0)<0\) determine the entire sign pattern, giving a nonpositive disk of area \(\rho/2<183/100\). The exact rational checker was executed from the actual package directory. No finite sampling is used to prove the global statement.

value.rationale: The exact negative-area minimum for planar self-Fourier eigenfunctions was posed as a natural quantitative uncertainty problem in 2026. A published sharp low-degree result suggests a natural false extrapolation of minimum 2; the explicit degree-sixteen witness rigorously breaks that finite-band barrier, giving a useful quantitative unrestricted upper bound <1.83 and an exact entire-sign-set certificate. The work does not assert a global optimum or nonradial classification.
